title: AOI-Net: Structural Face AOI-Guided Eye-Gaze Track Representation Learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
abstract: arXiv:2608.29289v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Eye-movement tracking has emerged as a promising non-invasive approach to Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) screening, with systematic differences in attentional allocation and revisit behaviors observed during socially interactive tasks. Existing computational methods typically characterize eye-movements using discrete gaze trajectories and fixation events, yielding representations dominated by short-range temporal dynamics and limiting models that primarily emphasize long-range dependencies. Meanwhile, gaze behavior is naturally organized across semantically meaningful Areas of Interest (AOIs), whose attention allocation and transitions provide important structural cues, yet their relationships are rarely modeled explicitly. To address these limitations, we propose a structural face AOI-guided Eye-Gaze Track Network (AOI-Net) that jointly models short-term temporal dynamics and AOI-level structural organization. translated_abstract: 眼动追踪已成为自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）筛查中一种有前景的无创方法，在社会互动任务中可以观察到注意分配和回视行为的系统性差异。现有的计算方法通常使用离散的注视轨迹和注视点事件来表征眼动，所得到的表征以短程时间动态为主，且限制了主要强调长程依赖关系的模型。与此同时，注视行为天然地组织在具有语义意义的兴趣区（AOI）之中，其注意分配与转换提供了重要的结构线索，但这些关系很少被显式建模。为解决上述局限，我们提出了一种结构化面部AOI引导的眼动轨迹网络（AOI-Net），该网络联合建模短程时间动态与AOI级别的结构组织。通过网络门控机制……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出AOI-Net，通过结构化面部兴趣区（AOI）引导的眼动轨迹表征学习，联合建模短程时间动态与AOI级别的结构组织，从而提升自闭症谱系障碍的检测效果。
en_tdlr: AOI-Net learns eye-gaze track representations guided by structural face AOIs, jointly modeling short-term temporal dynamics and AOI-level structural organization to improve autism spectrum disorder detection.
